references.text: The instructions for building the courtyard around the tabernacle and the altar, which Moses now completes in 40:33.
The description of how the courtyard was actually made with its hangings and gates.
The instruction regarding the screen for the gate of the courtyard (מָסַךְ שַׁעַר הֶחָצֵר) which Moses sets up here.
The confirmation that all the work on the tabernacle was completed just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
God's command to Moses to set up the courtyard and hang the screen for the gate.
Solomon finished (וַיְכַל) the construction of the temple, parallel to Moses who finished the tabernacle.
Hiram completed all the work he did for King Solomon, a similar conclusion to Moses' completion.
God finished (וַיְכַל) his work of creation, a parallel to Moses finishing the tabernacle as God's dwelling on earth.
The book of Hebrews describes the earthly tabernacle with its courtyard as a shadow of the heavenly sanctuary.
Both verses document different phases in the same event where Moses completes the setting up of the tabernacle.
Numbers 7:1 confirms and continues the sequence of events immediately after the completion mentioned in Exodus 40:33.
Both verses are parts of the same sequential process of setting up that leads to the completion in 40:33.
Both verses emphasize Moses' total obedience by confirming that everything was done exactly as the Lord had commanded.
This is a clear typological parallel between the completion of the tabernacle under Moses and the temple under Solomon.
